synopsis: Mining3 identifies a verification gap in mining collision avoidance: end users cannot easily verify suppliers’ reliability and functionality claims [f396, f687]. Mining3 and EMESRT emphasize field verification and site-specific baselines, in tension with automotive simulation advocates who argue that simulation can carry most of the statistical burden [f1122]. Mining3 delivered ACARP project C26028 in January 2021; the proximity-detection testing framework is a shared physical test protocol, not a simulator [f15627, f16088, f16119]. Access to ACARP and Mining3 methods, alongside MOSH specifications, test sites, a qualified independent body, and traceability, is identified as critical to shared frameworks and independent review [f1057].
